pairs.registryProposal: effort-calibration and policy-governance both assume the routing table is the system's own calibrated artifact. BYOM is a different animal: an operator-authored policy over which providers their own installation may use. The standard's demand that every entry cite its measurement is right for the vendor's class table and unenforceable for a user's allow-list. Suggest the golden path distinguish the calibrated class→tier→effort table (measured, dated, one authority) from operator policy layered over it (validated as data, versioned, diffed) — the governance half applies to both, the calibration half only to the first.

pairs.subject: agent-chaining
pairs.evidence: src/i18n/generated/types.ts:13467 — the chain_stop vocabulary is thirteen error-shaped tokens with no success-shaped stop (no completed), no cancelled, and no condition_unevaluable distinct from predicate_unmet, so a chain that ended naturally and a chain whose predicate could not be evaluated are not spellable.

techniques.evidence: src/i18n/generated/types.ts:13467 — the closed set (depth_limit, handoff_suppressed, cycle_detected, predicate_unmet, outside_window, malformed_config, cas_lost, quarantined, publish_failed, budget_exceeded, breadth_exceeded, healing_abandoned, healing_capped) covers the machinery-side family unusually well but carries no completed, no cancelled and no unevaluable, so 'the graph chose to stop' cannot be told from 'the chain finished' and the collapse of unevaluable into predicate_unmet reproduces the lie the evaluator refuses. The one-authority half is also only mitigated, not met: chainStopReasons.parity.test.ts:15 re-types the Rust consts by hand and compares that copy to en.json, so the guard checks two hand-maintained lists rather than its target — the test's own header (:4) records why (reason_token crosses ts-rs as a raw String, and tokenLabel falls back to printing the raw snake_case token behind a DEV-only warn).

src/i18n/__tests__/chainStopReasons.parity.test.ts:37 — the only structure asserted is a label catalog; no handoff envelope, compartment bound or receiving validation door appears in this context.

src/i18n/generated/types.ts:13468 — depth_limit and cycle_detected exist here only as labels for stops recorded elsewhere; the static detection pass and the runtime depth bound live in the Rust chain engine, outside these paths.
src/i18n/generated/types.ts:13471 — predicate_unmet is a rendered outcome, not an evaluator; no trigger mode is declared and no predicate is evaluated in this context.
src/i18n/__tests__/useTranslatedError.test.ts:15 — nothing in this context mints, forwards or rolls up a chain identity; the files hold a translation catalog and its guards.

pairs.registryProposal: Upward lesson worth an application entry rather than a correction: the technique predicts that a mature stop vocabulary grows a second, machinery-side family, and this repo landed six of the exact reasons it names — publish_failed (event publish failed after the edge was claimed), cas_lost (a concurrent evaluator won the race), quarantined (a repeatedly-failing edge), malformed_config (a guard's stored configuration found corrupt), handoff_suppressed (a stand-down rule because another driver owns the flow) and outside_window — arrived at independently. The token names are worth citing in the applications layer as a real-world spelling of that family. The same file also supplies a measured counter-example to the one-authority rule's usual remedy: because the token crosses the Rust/TS boundary as a raw String, the only available guard is a hand-mirrored parity test that cannot see its target (chainStopReasons.parity.test.ts:15) — a case where 'one authority' needs a codegen'd enum, not a test, and the standard could say so.
